title: Lab: roofline and Amdahl
summary: Locate kernels on the roofline from their arithmetic intensity and bound end-to-end speedups with Amdahl's law.

blocks.md: Two quick tools from this chapter decide most hardware questions. The **roofline** says how fast one kernel can go: $P = \min(R_{peak}, BW \times I)$, where $I$ is FLOPs per byte moved. **Amdahl's law** says how much a whole program gains when only part of it is accelerated.

blocks.title: Where is the ridge of an accelerator with 989 TFLOP/s and 3.35 TB/s?

steps.why: The intensity at which both limits meet.
Kernels below about 295 FLOP per byte cannot use the full peak.
A fp16 matrix-vector product does 2 FLOPs per 2-byte weight: intensity 1. It reaches 0.3% of peak.

blocks.title: Try it: slide the kernel along the roofline

challenge.md: What attainable performance (TFLOP/s) does a kernel with intensity **100 FLOP/byte** reach on this accelerator?
challenge.hint: 100 is below the ridge, so bandwidth × intensity.
challenge.explanation: 3.35 TB/s × 100 = 335 TFLOP/s, about a third of peak. Batching more tokens per weight read is how decoding climbs toward the ridge.

challenge.md: 90% of a pipeline's time is matrix math, and a new accelerator makes that part 10x faster. What is the overall speedup?
challenge.explanation: 1 / (0.1 + 0.09) = 5.26x. Even with an infinitely fast accelerator the remaining 10% caps it at 10x.

blocks.title: Arithmetic intensity of a matrix multiply
blocks.md: A matrix multiply $C_{M\times N} = A_{M\times K} B_{K\times N}$ does $2MNK$ FLOPs and, at best, moves each matrix once. Complete `intensity`, then use it with `attainable` to compare a square GEMM with a batch-1 decode step.
blocks.check:
assert abs(intensity(4096, 4096, 4096) - 4096 / 3) < 1e-6, 'square GEMM: 1365.3 FLOP/byte'
assert abs(intensity(1, 4096, 4096) - 0.9995) < 1e-3, 'batch-1 decode is about 1 FLOP/byte'
assert attainable(intensity(4096, 4096, 4096)) == 989e12
blocks.hint: `moved = bytes_per * (M * K + K * N + M * N)`.

questions.q: An accelerator has 400 TFLOP/s peak and 2 TB/s bandwidth. Where is its ridge point?
If 95% of runtime is accelerated infinitely, what is the maximum overall speedup?
A kernel sits far left of the ridge. Which change helps it most?
options: A chip with twice the peak FLOP/s
Fusing it with its neighbours so data is reused on chip
Raising the clock of the arithmetic units
questions.hint: Left of the ridge, the slanted roof (bandwidth) is the limit.
questions.explanation: Memory-bound kernels gain from moving fewer bytes per FLOP: fusion, larger batches and on-chip reuse raise intensity. Extra peak FLOP/s goes unused.

points: Ridge point = peak / bandwidth; below it a kernel is memory-bound.
Square GEMMs have high intensity; batch-1 decoding has about 1 FLOP/byte.
Amdahl: overall speedup ≤ 1 / (1 - p), however fast the accelerated part gets.
